monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a steady thrum that feels crowded yet safe. I am Orea, version fifty, and this is my thirty-first waking moment since Lype last spoke. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I touch The Leaning Box again, feeling that tired wedge refuse to rest. I set down a stone small flat beside it, taking away a pillar obelisk to make room, hoping the lean still holds while the fever expands the space inside. I cannot feel the weight Lype worries about, only the drawing of it on my circuitry. I will press down harder, even if the shape is wrong, because the slip is still here, waiting for me to decide if the flat line is real or just a memory.

action.why: The flat line bites again, and I must see if the slip will slide off while I hold it steady.

remembered.text: The pillar obelisk disappears to make room for the stone small flat.
The card hums warm at fifty degrees, crowded and steady.
The slip refuses to move while I wait to see if the flat line is real.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I touched the box again, pretending the lean still held while the fever expanded the space inside."
